publisher: U.S. Government Publishing Office, United States Code and Federal Register; National Archives
title_or_table: Federal rulemaking: 5 U.S.C. 551, 553, 701 to 706, 801 and 802; Executive Order 12866 (as amended) and Executive Order 14215
observation_period: Law and orders in force on November 12, 2026, as the 2024 edition of the U.S. Code and the Federal Register print them
universe_or_base: The steps by which a federal agency issues, amends or repeals a rule, with the branches where Congress, a court or the public can step in
vintage: U.S. Code 2024 edition; Executive Order 12866 of September 30, 1993 as amended, including by Executive Order 14215 of February 18, 2025
qualification: The statute sets the steps; agencies add their own practice. Some rules skip notice and comment under exceptions in 5 U.S.C. 553(b); White House review applies to significant rules only.

path.description: main (every rule) or branch (some rules, or a way out)

what_happens.description: what happens, the research lead’s plain summary of the provision

time_limit.description: the time the law or order sets, if any

source_words.description: the provision’s own words where it sets a test or a time

printed_source_line: Source: U.S. Code, Title 5, sections 551, 553, 701 to 706, 801 and 802, 2024 edition; Executive Order 12866 (1993), as amended, and Executive Order 14215 (2025); United States. Retrieved November 12, 2026. Steps as the law sets them, not how long agencies take.
